image_description: A dimly lit interior view of a prison cell block, featuring two levels of walkways with metal railings on either side. The walls are distressed concrete or plaster with peeling paint. In the background, vertical bars of cell doors are visible. The perspective leads down a central corridor.

The design is strictly functional, repetitive, and stark, fitting the utilitarian description.
The visible barriers are solid metal railings and bars, not chain-link or palisade fencing (which are typically exterior).

artifact_observations.location: Walls on both left and right sides
artifact_observations.reasoning: The texture of the peeling paint and grime appears slightly repetitive and 'smudged' rather than naturally chaotic, typical of AI generation trying to simulate decay.
The metal railing on the upper right seems to merge into the wall without a clear mounting bracket or support structure, appearing to float or fuse slightly.
The arched structural beams on the ceiling show slight inconsistency in their curve and alignment relative to the linear perspective of the floor.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the scene is correctly classified as a prison/correctional facility and not a generic industrial hallway or mine shaft.
To verify the depth consistency of the long corridor and ensure the parallel lines of the walkways converge correctly without warping.
To check for fusion artifacts where the thin metal bars meet the walls or floor, ensuring they are distinct objects.

focus_areas: Structural integrity of metal railings and their connections to walls
Consistency of perspective in the long corridor
Correct identification of the environment as a correctional facility
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'floating' nature of the railings. AI often struggles with thin structural elements like bars, causing them to blend into backgrounds. Verify if the classifier distinguishes this from a generic 'abandoned building' which might lack the specific security features (bars) required for the 'prison' label.
